nodes.prompt: Read the protected task and repository and research. Return an additive desired-state proposal matching intent-proposal.schema.json: users, journeys (id, actor, entry, steps, acceptance_ids), requirements, nonfunctional_requirements, ux_expectations, technical_constraints, integration_constraints, security_requirements, compatibility_requirements, performance_requirements, failure_behaviour, edge_cases, dependencies, assumptions, milestones, testing_criteria, definition_of_done, acceptance, nongoals, questions. Preserve every original goal, acceptance ID and constraint; do not weaken intent. Include executable acceptance checks where grounded, and explicit unresolved questions rather than inventing product decisions. The host accepts the proposal before planning. Do not change product files. Keep every original acceptance statement byte-for-byte with its stable ID and required flag. Fill in a missing executable check or missing write bounds when evidence supports it, but never change an existing check or bound. Derived checks and scope are subject to the host initial intent-confirmation transaction.

Turn the approved specification into ordered vertical slices and stack.json module boundaries without changing production files. Read execution-repair.json and graph/checkpoint files when present. Use graph_mutate to create, split, replace or supersede implementation tasks and their dependencies when the strategy must change. Every task references protected goalIds; revisions require triggering evidence and an explanation of what differs. Never alter safety nodes or intent.
